_comment: Binds the committed confidential SP1 guest ELFs to the verifying keys they must be deployed with. Two ELFs from one `cargo prove build`: elf/cxfer-guest (the settle guest → program_vkey, immutable PROGRAM_VKEY) and elf/reflection-prover (the Bitcoin-state relay prover → bitcoin_relay_vkey, immutable BITCOIN_RELAY_VKEY). verify-vkey-pin.sh asserts both sha256s on every PR. A rebuild that changes either ELF MUST regenerate its vkey + update this file IN THE SAME COMMIT, then redeploy ConfidentialPool with the new immutable vkey — otherwise every settle (resp. every attestBitcoinStateProven) reverts. Each vkey is the key a REAL Groth16 proof of THAT ELF verifies against on-chain (test/ConfidentialSwapProofReal.t.sol, test/ConfidentialReflectionProofReal.t.sol). The two share cxfer-core, so a cxfer-core change rebuilds BOTH — committing the ELFs is what keeps the prover box running the pinned bytes rather than a drifting rebuild.
reflection_elf_note: gen5 deployed reflection prover: built from 9e043071 (the ETH_CALL_OUTBOX re-pin); settle guest: 4a425f1d
_btc_pool_note: elf/btc-pool-prover (DESIGN-btc-shielded-pool.md) is an independent guest, not part of the settle/reflection lockstep group: it proves one T_BTC_SPEND and commits abi.encode(uint16 1, bytes32 root, bytes32 keccak(body)). Its proofs are verified locally by Bitcoin-side indexers with sp1_verifier::Groth16Verifier against the SP1 Groth16 key (btc-pool-verify); no Ethereum contract verifies it and nothing on Ethereum depends on this vkey. The vkey is derived with `cargo prove vkey --elf elf/btc-pool-prover`, which needs no prover backend: the ELF alone determines it. The Groth16 key is byte-identical to the one behind the mainnet SP1 v6.1.0 verifier leaf 0xb69f2584CBcFf99a58C4e7002E8b89Af54a6f4e2: btc_pool_groth16_verifier_hash is its VERIFIER_HASH (sha256 of sp1-verifier groth16_vk.bin) and btc_pool_groth16_vk_root its VK_ROOT.
_lockstep: X-4: ETH_REFLECTION_VKEY + ETH_GENESIS_SYNC_COMMITTEE (reflect.rs), BATCH_VK_SHA256 (groth16.rs) and the reflection vkey/sha/eth_reflection_vkey above must all be regenerated from ONE prover-host checkpoint. verify-lockstep-pins.sh hashes the six together and compares against lockstep_checkpoint; a partial rotation is fail-closed at run time but miserable to diagnose, so it is caught here instead. After any rotation re-record with verify-lockstep-pins.sh --record in the SAME commit.
_vkey_authority: program_vkey + bitcoin_relay_vkey are the AUTHORITATIVE deploy vkeys for the committed ELFs; guest_state below is descriptive prose only (it has lagged the fields before). These four fields are the ONLY occurrences of those key names in this file — every history block uses deployed_*-prefixed names so it can never shadow them. The vkey<->ELF binding is enforced mechanically at prove time by the EXPECT_VKEY / ELF_VKEY_PIN guard in exec-prove.rs (program_vkey) and exec-reflect-prove.rs (bitcoin_relay_vkey), and at deploy time by DeployConfidentialPool's require(vkey == .program_vkey). After any ELF rebuild, derive both vkeys on the prover host and reconcile every field here in the same commit.

_reprove_2026_07_23: Reprove for the wrap-fusion + hardening round. Guest changes: OP_WRAP_LP(32) and OP_WRAP_SWAP(33) fuse a public deposit into LP-add / swap so an external wallet reaches a shielded position in one settle; fee_is_quantized enforces a coarse fee ladder in-guest so a relay cannot fingerprint a payer with an odd-valued PUBLIC FeePayment; cdp_topup_msg binds owner authority to OP_CDP_TOPUP (a note carrying a victim's owner LABEL could otherwise replace their position and censor them into liquidation); eth-reflection finality advance tightened >= to strict > (a >= gate let a fabricated bootstrap execution root ride in behind a genuine finality update that did not advance the slot). Superseded: settle 0x003a21ba, bitcoin_relay 0x00af1dd7, eth_reflection 0x00583f05. LOCKSTEP: rebuilding the eth-reflection ELF rotates its RECURSION digest (vk.hash_u32()), which the reflection guest embeds as ETH_REFLECTION_VKEY and checks via verify_sp1_proof. The first rebuild of this round left that constant stale, so the reflection guest would have rejected every Mode-B proof; the constant was rotated and the reflection guest rebuilt, moving bitcoin_relay_vkey 0x001e0f7b -> 0x00580f84. The settle guest is unaffected (digest lives only in reflect.rs) and its vkey is unchanged. SETTLE ROTATION 2: the LP/route multi-note + change-output work (and a CDP-mint fix that stopped an unconditional debt-commitment read forcing a zero-debt bond to invent a curve point) changed the settle guest again — program_vkey 0x0081360d -> 0x00014cc4. eth_reflection and reflection-prover rebuilt byte-identical, so the recursion digest and bitcoin_relay_vkey are unaffected.
_reprove_2026_08_26_swapbatch_tips: Reprove for the swapbatch enablement + gasless relay-tips round. Settle guest: OP_SWAP_BLIND (31) un-panicked (real prover-blind AMM clearing now runs) and per-asset relay tips armed (per-intent tip read + bound into the PoK ctx, both fail-closed asserts removed) — program_vkey 0x00014cc4 -> 0x0082db7e (elf sha 6813ca52). Reflection guest: Track-C fold_swap_batch (0x2F) re-armed from no-op — bitcoin_relay_vkey 0x00580f84 -> 0x00edafc6 (reflection elf sha 1e2a75fb). eth-reflection ELF unchanged, so ETH_REFLECTION_VKEY / ETH_GENESIS_SYNC_COMMITTEE (reflect.rs) and BATCH_VK_SHA256 (groth16.rs) are all unchanged; only lockstep_checkpoint is re-recorded because two of its inputs (bitcoin_relay_vkey, reflection_elf_sha256) rotated. Built non-Docker on the RunPod prover host (docker-in-docker blocked by the pod's user-namespace restriction; the confidential guests have no docker-canonical CI — that scaffolding covers only the legacy tETH program). vkeys derived via harnesses/vkey.rs (client.setup(elf).verifying_key().bytes32()).
_reprove_2026_09_16_v1_final: Reprove for the v1-final round. Guest changes: a completeness gate on burn-deposit provenance so an incomplete provenance blob can no longer let the fold skip silently; the Bitcoin-homed spend-authorization message (btc_note_spend_msg) now length-prefixes its variable-length output-leaf list, making the signed encoding injective by construction instead of relying on a field-width coincidence (every existing Bitcoin-homed-input fixture needed a fresh signature under the new encoding); chunked handling for large reflection catch-up batches; swap-batch range proofs upgraded to real BP+ proofs on both the settle and reflection lanes; a cross-generation retirement path (ReflectionLib.retireCheck) so a successor pool recognizes notes already retired by a prior generation; a farm-bond guest fix; farm-refund's launcher authorization is now verified as a real BIP-340 signature over the refund terms rather than trusted as an off-chain convention; and a broad comment-cleanup pass with no functional change. Rebuilt on the RunPod prover host (tacit-confidence, cargo-prove sp1 4809e79) — settle program_vkey 0x00711089 -> 0x00696320 (elf sha c973893d, 1675320 bytes), reflection bitcoin_relay_vkey 0x0097a385 -> 0x001dfdc1 (elf sha 58e7c474, 1308168 bytes). eth-reflection ELF/vkey and ETH_REFLECTION_VKEY/ETH_GENESIS_SYNC_COMMITTEE/BATCH_VK_SHA256 are unchanged this round (confirmed by a zero source diff on contracts/sp1/eth-reflection), so lockstep_checkpoint moves only from the reflection-side rotation. All 35 settle + 2 reflection Groth16 fixtures were regenerated against the rebuilt ELFs on the Succinct network and reconciled in the same pass as this pin update; a stale LP-add fixture generator (nested d/sSig/kernel fields instead of the harness's top-level dA/dB/sSig/aKernel/bKernel shape) and a stale crosslane signature (pre-dating the length-prefix change) were fixed as part of getting those two fixtures to regenerate cleanly. Several settle harnesses whose Groth16 branch used local native-gnark CPU proving were switched to network proving in the same round, matching the pattern already used by the rest of the harness set — the box's cgroup memory cap could not fit some of the larger circuits' local proof generation.
_reprove_2026_09_16_v2_final_audit: Reprove for the pre-lock audit round, replacing the (INCORRECT) _pending_rebuild_2026_09_16_final_audit note below, which claimed the settle guest was untouched — empirically false, established by rebuilding BOTH ELFs from the current source on the RunPod prover host (tacit-confidence, cargo-prove sp1 4809e79) and comparing the derived vkeys against the v1-final pin, not by re-reading the audit's own verdict. REFLECTION (as the audit correctly identified): contracts/sp1/confidential/src/reflect.rs now refuses outright any burn-deposit provenance blob that carries pool-membership-shortcut leaves — a tree leaf commits no outpoint, so such a leaf let the DAG accept a prover-asserted (outpoint, commitment) pair unbound to any real UTXO, letting any tracked note's owner mint against it repeatedly; and ETH_CALL_OUTBOX was rotated from the predecessor generation's outbox to this generation's own freshly-mined vanity address (0x00000000526e89e1b461ca5631f0d3489a65ccb9) so the reverse ETH->BTC lane never depends on infrastructure outside this deployment — bitcoin_relay_vkey 0x001dfdc1 -> 0x004002de (elf sha 51269e2f, 1306640 bytes). Both-sided REFLECT-1 test RE-RUN against this ELF via reflect-execute (see readiness-gate.sh CONFIRMED_SOUND_REFL_VKEYS 0x004002de entry): CONSERVING control folds with DIGEST_MATCH against the JS assembler, NON-CONSERVING case skips with no panic — unchanged from the prior generation. SETTLE (the audit's claim does not hold): contracts/sp1/confidential/src/main.rs differentiated OP_WRAP_TRANSFER's opening-sigma domain tag from plain OP_WRAP's (both were b"tacit-wrap-intent-v1"; OP_WRAP_TRANSFER now uses b"tacit-wraptransfer-intent-v1", matching dapp/confidential-pool-ux.js's wrap-and-send builder and tests/gen-confidential-wraptransfer-fixture.mjs, verified in lockstep) — this alone is a real, non-dead-code change to the settle guest's own dispatch, since a single compiled RISC-V ELF has ONE vkey for its entire program regardless of which opcode arm changed. (Separately, swap_batch.rs's fold_swap_batch changed too — a settler-malformed swap-batch receipt now REFUNDS instead of skipping — but the settle ELF's own compiler output confirms fold_swap_batch is dead code from main.rs's dispatch ("warning: function `fold_swap_batch` is never used" on the settle build), so that specific function is genuinely reflection-only; it is main.rs's own OP_WRAP_TRANSFER tag, OP_SWAP_BLIND per-receipt BP+ range-proof read+check via swap_blind.rs, and OP_FARM_BOND's leg_auth now unconditionally witnessed instead of defaulting to `owner` when unauthenticated, that make the settle ELF genuinely different from what v1-final pinned.) program_vkey 0x00696320 -> 0x0024bd06 (elf sha 3d173e8f, 1675600 bytes). SETTLE FIXTURES: all 35 committed settle *_groth16.json fixtures were regenerated against the rebuilt ELF on the Succinct network (EXPECT_VKEY-guarded) and now bind to 0x0024bd06, closing what was initially a known gap in this round. wraptransfer_op.json was regenerated first (via tests/gen-confidential-wraptransfer-fixture.mjs) since its intent signature is over the new domain tag; every other op's existing op.json witness was reused as-is (no wire-format change) and simply re-proven under the new ELF. The adaptor-claim/lock/refund, cdp-mint/close/liquidate/topup and cbtc-mint fixtures (8 total), whose test-file doc comments still cite the STALE contracts/sp1/confidential/harnesses/exec-gap.rs ("DO NOT USE FOR FIXTURE REGENERATION"), were in fact regenerated via the dedicated non-stale per-op harnesses that already exist alongside it (exec-adaptorclaim.rs / exec-adaptorlock.rs / exec-adaptorrefund.rs / exec-cdpmint.rs / exec-cdpclose.rs / exec-cdpliquidate.rs / exec-cdptopup.rs / exec-cbtcmint.rs, each reading its op's real fixtures/*_op.json in the guest's own io::read order) — exec-gap.rs was not touched and remains stale/unused. verify-vkey-pin.sh is fully green (all 35 settle + 2 reflection fixtures bind to a pinned vkey); DeployConfidentialPool.s.sol / DeployV1Suite.s.sol / DeployV1SuiteCreateX.s.sol DEFAULT_VKEY and harnesses/build.rs PINNED_ELF_SHA256 were rotated in lockstep.
_reprove_2026_09_17_v1_final_lock: Reprove for the v1-final PRE-LOCK closing security review (largest of the cycle; findings in scratchpad/audit-2026-09-16/NOTES.md). cxfer-core changed (transfer-kernel domain separation closing C-1 re-type theft; rebase drain-gate H-1 fix; eth sync-committee chaining R1; pending burn-deposit set R2; deposit-class leaf owner=outpoint-key R3; AXFER asset_input_count parser P-2; AMM refund-on-extra-input F-5; OP_SWAP_BLIND aggregate-kernel redesign M-2; BTC-call chain-id binding), so ALL THREE ELFs were rebuilt in the required order: eth-reflection first, then reflect.rs's ETH_REFLECTION_VKEY was re-pinned to the fresh eth-reflection recursion digest BEFORE rebuilding reflection-prover, then confidential-pool-prover (settle) last. Built on the RunPod prover host (tacit-confidence, cargo-prove sp1 4809e79) — settle program_vkey 0x0024bd06 -> 0x006cd47f (elf sha f7bc327d, 1681088 bytes), reflection bitcoin_relay_vkey 0x004002de -> 0x00f8c4dc (elf sha 6b184852, 1340312 bytes), eth-reflection eth_reflection_vkey 0x00d5e2a3 -> 0x00ca8171 (elf sha 5fb193b5, 2327032 bytes; hash_u32 recursion digest [1698740370,761725306,1843717690,1218893588,786585592,423901230,1310805602,795535986] pinned into reflect.rs's ETH_REFLECTION_VKEY). GENESIS SYNC-COMMITTEE RE-PIN (recommended by the re-audit, done this round): the prior anchor (period 1800, slot 14,745,600) only had beacon light-client update-retention runway to roughly 2026-12-03; re-pinned via eth_prove's [genesis-capture] against a LIVE mainnet finalized checkpoint (finalized period 1859 at capture time) to the period-1859 boundary, slot 15,228,928, sync_committee_root 0xbadc9e8edde525d58ea8df0f258da9768be4f2d68add89d8c55b03c217c4f5ec — pushes the runway to roughly period 1987 (~2027-02). ETH_GENESIS_VALIDATORS_ROOT (the actual beacon chain-genesis constant, permanent) is unchanged. deployments/1.json ethGenesisSlot/ethGenesisSyncCommittee updated to match. BATCH_VK_SHA256 (groth16.rs, the baked swap-batch ceremony VK) is UNCHANGED — the ceremony did not rotate, only cxfer-core/main.rs's OUTER kernel wiring around it did — so lockstep_checkpoint moves from all three vkey/sha rotations plus the ETH_GENESIS_SYNC_COMMITTEE change, not from BATCH_VK_SHA256. Disk on the box was 85% full (9.2G free) from ~36G of stale dated build-cache snapshots under /workspace/cargo-target from prior reprove rounds; cleaned before this round's builds. See scratchpad/audit-2026-09-16/NOTES.md for the full fixture-regen ledger and cost/time accounting.
_pending_rebuild_2026_09_16_final_audit_: REFLECTION ELF REBUILD REQUIRED BEFORE DEPLOY. The final pre-lock audit changed contracts/sp1/confidential/src/reflect.rs (a burn-deposit provenance blob that carries pool-membership shortcut leaves is now refused outright — a tree leaf commits no outpoint, so such a leaf seeded the DAG with a prover-asserted (outpoint, commitment) pair that any tracked note's owner could mint against repeatedly) and contracts/sp1/confidential/src/swap_batch.rs (a settler-malformed receipt cross-curve sigma / range proof now REFUNDS the batch instead of skipping it, mirrored in dapp/confidential-swapbatch.js). The committed elf/reflection-prover (sha 58e7c474…) predates both edits and no longer matches its source: rebuild reflection-prover on the prover host, re-derive bitcoin_relay_vkey, re-record lockstep_checkpoint (verify-lockstep-pins.sh --record), regenerate the two reflection Groth16 fixtures, and update reflection_elf_sha256/reflection_elf_bytes/bitcoin_relay_vkey here IN THE SAME COMMIT. The settle guest (main.rs, cxfer-core) is untouched by the audit, so program_vkey and the 35 settle fixtures stand; the settle harness exec-swapblind.rs gained the out_range_proof write the already-pinned settle ELF reads. SUPERSEDED by _reprove_2026_09_16_v2_final_audit above — this note's central claim ("the settle guest ... is untouched by the audit") was verified FALSE by an actual rebuild+vkey-compare; kept only so the incorrect claim is visible next to its correction rather than silently deleted.
